title: UK VC bets big on AI, leaving other sectors starved for cash

content_html:
Leah Hodgson

Fri, August 7, 2026 at 6:32 AM EDT 2 min read

Kanishka Narayan, UK's Minister for Artificial Intelligence

Hindustan Times/Getty Images

AI is dominating the UK's venture market this year at the expense of its legacy verticals.

Investment in UK startups totaled £14.4 billion (about $19.4 billion) in the first half of the year, according to PitchBook's 2026 UK Private Capital Breakdown, already reaching almost three-quarters of last year's deal value.

Of that deal value, more than 70% has been directed to AI startups. Almost 40% of overall European AI funding was claimed by UK startups in H1.

The UK has made AI central to its growth plans, with startups a key part of that strategy. In April, the government launched a £500 million sovereign AI fund, which has already backed companies such as AI lab Ineffable Intelligence and drug developer Isomorphic Labs.

In June, the government announced a £1.1 billion AI hardware plan to back companies developing chips and semiconductor technologies, including startups such as Olix, which received funding from the Sovereign AI fund and recently raised a $312 million Series B, and Fractile.

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham's team is looking to overhaul the country's AI strategy, the Financial Times reported, with a focus on tech sovereignty and on appointing Kanishka Narayan as the UK's first dedicated AI minister.

This article appeared as part of The Europe Pitch newsletter. Sign up here

The wave of funding going to AI has left many other sectors bereft of capital, including historical mainstays such as fintech. According to the Breakdown, funding for the latter had not even reached £1 billion by the end of June and is currently pacing 75% below last year's total. Mobile, which in previous years ranked third by annual deal value, is also tracking around 80% below historical norms.

The UK's heavy skew toward AI raises concerns about concentration risk, particularly because much of the funding is focused on just a handful of companies. Almost 60% of H1's overall deal value came from just 18 deals, despite more than 1,100 rounds closing. Nine out of 10 of the largest deals were for an AI startup.

Concerns are already mounting in the public sector about the sustainability of AI spending and the pace of corporate adoption. If a market correction were to occur, the UK's ecosystem would be heavily affected.

This article originally appeared on PitchBook News

卡尼什卡·纳拉扬 (Kanishka Narayan)，英国人工智能大臣

印度斯坦时报/盖蒂图片社

人工智能今年在英国风险投资市场占据主导地位，但其传统垂直行业却受到了损害。

根据 PitchBook 的 2026 年英国私人资本细分数据，今年上半年英国初创企业的投资总额为 144 亿英镑（约合 194 亿美元），已达到去年交易价值的近四分之三。

在这些交易价值中，超过 70% 流向了人工智能初创公司。 上半年，英国初创公司获得了欧洲人工智能融资总额的近 40%。

英国已将人工智能作为其增长计划的核心，而初创企业是该战略的关键部分。 今年 4 月，政府推出了 5 亿英镑的主权人工智能基金，该基金已经支持了人工智能实验室 Ineffable Intelligence 和药物开发商 Isomorphic Labs 等公司。

6 月，政府宣布了一项 11 亿英镑的人工智能硬件计划，以支持开发芯片和半导体技术的公司，其中包括 Olix 和 Fractile 等初创公司，Olix 获得了 Sovereign AI 基金的资助，最近筹集了 3.12 亿美元的 B 轮融资。

据英国《金融时报》报道，新首相安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）的团队正在寻求彻底改革该国的人工智能战略，重点关注技术主权，并任命卡尼什卡·纳拉扬（Kanishka Narayan）为英国首位专门负责人工智能的部长。

本文作为欧洲推介时事通讯的一部分出现。 在这里注册

流向人工智能的资金浪潮使许多其他行业失去了资本，包括金融科技等历史支柱行业。 据Breakdown报道，截至6月底，后者的资金还不到10亿英镑，目前比去年的总额低了75%。 移动领域在年度交易额方面前几年排名第三，但现在也比历史水平低了 80% 左右。

英国对人工智能的严重倾斜引发了人们对集中风险的担忧，特别是因为大部分资金都集中在少数公司身上。 尽管完成了 1,100 多轮交易，但上半年总交易价值的近 60% 仅来自 18 笔交易。 最大的 10 笔交易中有 9 笔是针对人工智能初创公司的。

公共部门已经越来越担心人工智能支出的可持续性和企业采用的速度。 如果市场出现调整，英国的生态系统将受到严重影响。
